newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks up but below highs ahead of US data.
newsitem.headline: French stocks up but below highs ahead of US data.

text.p: French shares were trading higher but below year highs at midsession, before a batch of U.S. economic data and the opening of Wall Street.

Dealers said the shares could extend their gains if Wall Street continued its advance but they worried that after yesterday's record of above 6,300 for the Dow Jones, there could be profit-taking and losses before the weekend.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 23.40 points or 1.05 percent at 2,241.58 at 1245 GMT after a year high of 2,247.43 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 21 at 2,247.
The French rise takes shares back to early 1994 levels. The historic high, at 2,360.98, was reached on February 2, 1994.
Data due today are U.S. October capacity utilisation, expected at 83 pct, and industrial production, seen up 0.2 percent, as well as September business inventories which are expected up 0.2 percent.
In France, the August seasonally-adjusted current account surplus rose to 10.40 billion francs.
* LVMH cancels losses on fears of a bidding war for U.S. firm DFS after a source said a possible KKR bid was conditional on LVMH withdrawing, which it did not intend.
* L'Oreal hits year high ahead of road show in Geneva, with traders seeing no clear reasons for the gains.
* Renault was 2.75 percent higher at 123.40 despite issuing a warning that truck losses could be higher than previously forecast.

The group said car sales in the third quarter rose 5.33 percent to 33.33 billion francs, but sales slid 10.1 percent in the commercial vehicles division to 6.36 billion. Stock market traders said the figures were better than they had expected. Car industry analysts said, however, there were signs of severe price cutting.
* Insurers UAP and AXA remain the biggest volume stocks after Thursday's resumption of trade following share swap merger. Over 3.3 million UAP shares and 944,000 UAP shares had traded by 1305 GMT.
* BNP, a large UAP shareholder, also rises in good volume. Dealers said the insurers merger put the financial sector back in play.

* Suez gains in good volume on newspaper report a long rumoured property-asset deal is now imminent. Dealers said that while Suez would take a capital loss on the deal, it would unshackle the group from its property woes.
